cultural.vision_reason: The image shows a hand-woven strip-woven cotton hammock (kpoikpoi) with typical Mende-style supplementary weft patterning in indigo, white and red — a classic Mende textile form used in daily life.

physical.title: hammock; textile
physical.summary: Hammock (kpoikpoi), formed of three wide strips about 23cm wide of hand-spun cotton, which have been hand-woven and hand-sewn together along the selvedges. The ends of the hammock are in white cotton, while the central area on all three strips is completely covered by weft-faced blocks of coloured cotton that form a pattern across the whole in red and two shades of indigo. Within these there are smaller areas with supplementary weft patterns float-woven in indigo and white cotton; some of these are in tapestry-weave. To the sides of the hammock have been sewn six other pieces of woven cloth intended to hang down as flaps (three a side) when the hammock was in use; these are also covered with weft-faced blocks of coloured cotton, and have decorative pompons at the ends. The warp ends of the hammock itself have hand-sewn hems.

cultural.vision_reason: A strip-woven cotton "country cloth" with nested geometric borders, hair-comb motifs, and lozenge panels — a classic Mende woven textile type from Sierra Leone, matching the museum's attribution.

physical.title: cloth
physical.summary: A woven cotton 'country cloth' made up of panels, approximately 20cms in width, stitched together.  The textile is decorated with a series of nested borders worked in natural un-dyed cotton, dark brown and sand-coloured dyed cotton.  The inner border features a repeated hair-comb motif and a geometric design that frames an un-dyed panel in the centre.  This panel features two lozenges with internal alternating geometric motifs. The top and bottom of the cloth has a fringe.

cultural.vision_reason: The image shows a striped-and-banded handwoven cotton strip cloth (kpoikpoi) with indigo and white weft-float diamond patterning, a well-known Mende display cloth type from Sierra Leone made of hand-woven narrow strips sewn together.

physical.title: cloth; textile
physical.summary: Display cloth (kpoikpoi), composed of 10 strips of hand-woven and hand-spun cotton, each about 15.5 cm, or 6 ½ inches wide, hand-sewn together along the selvedges. Each strip has a base of white cotton, which is crossed by double weft stripes of indigo. The main decoration is formed by three weft bands which run across the width of the whole cloth: these are in two shades of indigo, and include supplementary weft floats of white cotton that form a diamond pattern set against the light indigo ground weft background. At each end of the cloth is a continuous line in indigo, and the warp ends have been left as a fringe.

cultural.vision_reason: A handwoven strip-cloth blanket with narrow stripes and supplementary-weave diamond motifs in a central panel, composed of narrow strips machine-sewn selvedge to selvedge — a classic West African strip-weaving construction consistent with Mende textile tradition in Sierra Leone.

physical.title: cloth; blanket
physical.summary: Blanket; textile; furnishing; hand-woven cotton and synthetic fibres composed of seven narrow strips machine sewn selvedge to selvedge forming a rectangular shape with an unworked warp fringe. Plain weave; white and black machine spun cotton warp; dyed buff, brown, blue, green, light blue and cream cotton and wefts. The majority of the decoration is in bands that are part of the ground weave. These bands are in a number of combinations of the following colours: dyed buff, brown, blue, green, light blue and cream. There are also three bands which are decorated with supplementary weave: 1.Diamond based pattern in blue; 2.Diamond and polygon based pattern in blue; 3.Diamond based pattern in blue.

cultural.vision_reason: The image shows a hand-woven, hand-spun cotton strip-woven hammock (kpoikpoi) with striped and patterned panels, mounted on carved wooden poles — a classic Mende textile/craft object.

physical.title: hammock
physical.summary: Hammock (kpoikpoi), formed of three wide strips about 20cm wide of hand-spun cotton, which have been hand-woven and hand-sewn together along the selvedges. The base weave of the entire hammock is of hand-spun white cotton, used in both warp and weft. The ends of the hammock are left in white cotton, and they are mounted on two wooden poles for the bearers. These poles are hand carved with birds heads at each end and then varnished. In the central 50cm area on all three strips, the ground weave is decorated with six motifs in supplementary weft with a 'wine-glass' shape in dark indigo; the remaining space between these six shapes is occupied by coils of unspun wool. Arranged symmetrically on either side of this central band are coloured bands of decoration in supplementary weft using imported European thread of two shades of blue, black, yellow, green and red. To the sides of the hammock have been sewn a fringe of threads braided into tassels which were intended to hang down the sides when the hammock was in use.

cultural.vision_reason: A hand-woven narrow-strip cotton hammock with banded decoration and tasselled ends, a classic Mende/Sierra Leone textile craft object made and used by the people.

physical.title: hammock
physical.summary: Hammock; made of cotton, hand-woven in four narrow strips which have been sewn together along the selvedges. The cotton is mostly hand-spun and locally dyed, though the red and black appears to be European imported thread. The warp is of white cotton, and the weft uses a mixture of white, green, red and black cotton to form bands of decoration across the cloth. The two inner strips have a long area of white tufts of cotton along the centre; in the two outer strips these are replaced either by bands of decoration of the same kind as is seen at the ends of the cloth, or by designs in the shape of 'wine glasses' formed from discontinuous supplementary black thread. Along both sides a long fringe of white cotton openwork terminating in bobbles has been sewn on.
